_scenario: One "2d" PhysicsWorld on Rapier2dAdapter with Appendix A gravity, holding a static rectangle floor (top y = -3.5) and twelve dynamic 0.5 m boxes of mass 0.5 … 6 kg fanned across x = -5.5 … 5.5. A ForceFieldSystem at PRIORITY_FORCES (500) and a PhysicsSystem at PRIORITY_PHYSICS_SOLVE (600) share one SystemRegistry, driven 300 clean fixed steps of 1/60 s with an injected TimeState whose simulationTime is exactly step / 60. Four §27 fields, in registration order — dragField(0.35) as "acceleration", a time-only sin gust as "force", vortexField as "acceleration", radialField as "force" — each wrapped in one volumeField box centred (0, 2, 0) with half-extents (14, 5, 1), whose floor at y = -3 sits above the bodies' resting height of y = -3.25 so a settled body receives exactly (0, 0, 0) and §32 can put it to sleep. The per-step value is world.checksum() (§33's own checksum, not a re-derivation); summaryDigest is the D6 FNV-1a hasher over all 300 of them in step order.
_tier: same-runtime (§33), the same tier and the same reasons as golden/phase5.json: Rapier is compiled WebAssembly, state crosses the JS/wasm boundary as f64 → f32, and the wasm image is pinned per platform by the package manager. The field arithmetic adds its own runtime-bound inputs — vortexField and radialField call Math.sqrt, the gust calls Math.sin — so cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
